industry_aggregates.notes: Reported as 'total credit extended to Nigeria's private sector by Deposit Money Banks' for 2025 (vs. N689.98trn in 2024). Not confirmed whether this is an end-December balance or a full-year flow figure; a differing N730.2trn figure for the same year appeared in a related source, so treat as approximate. Not independently verified against a primary CBN Statistical Bulletin/FSR document.

Part of a fast-moving series through CBN's COVID-19 forbearance withdrawal: 7.51% (Dec 2025) -> 8.03% (Jan 2026) -> 9.85% (Feb 2026) -> 9.94% (Q1 2026), all above the CBN's 5% prudential ceiling. Earlier 2025 figures (~5.6% in April 2025) are now stale and should not be used alongside this one without noting the trend. Secondary-source citation of CBN data, not verified against a primary CBN document.

source.source_name: Vanguard News, citing CBN Q1 2026 forbearance-withdrawal reporting

Note this predates the sharp 2025-2026 rise recorded elsewhere in this file (7.51% Dec 2025 -> 9.94% Q1 2026) as CBN withdrew COVID-19 forbearance -- the gap between 4.50% (Dec 2024) and 7.51% (Dec 2025) is a real and significant one-year jump, not a data error.

industry_aggregates.notes: This is CBN's 'credit to the private sector' series (the figure Nigerian financial press consistently uses as the industry benchmark), which is narrower than 'total DMB gross loans outstanding' since it excludes credit to government/public sector -- not directly comparable to the 2025 total_gross_credit figure elsewhere in this file without accounting for that difference.
